# Talking to a mini-PC's embedded controller — EVO-X2 / Strix Halo EC notes

Field notes for people running AMD Strix Halo mini-PCs on Linux — the class of
box (GMKtec EVO-X2, Bosgame M5, FEVM FA-EX9: all the same Sixunited AXB35-02
board) whose firmware exposes no standard fan control: no hwmon PWM, no fan
tachometer, no ACPI fan object. The only lever is the Embedded Controller, and
the only documentation is what you can measure yourself. These notes restate
the canonical repo's register map, its two laws of EC writes, register
validation without vendor docs, and the re-assertion deployment pattern.

## Canonical links

- This repo: https://github.com/simongonzalezdc/resonant-evo-x2-ec-notes
- Canonical source: https://github.com/KyaniteLabs/evo-x2-ec (MIT) — the register map, validation scripts, and deploy units

## Key facts

- License: MIT
- Safety: the EC also runs thermal protection; registers were characterized
  empirically with no vendor documentation; writing unlisted registers is
  unwritten territory
- Every claim carries a provenance line pointing at the canonical repo's file
- Nothing here re-measures or re-brands anything

Relationship: community gift by Kyanite Labs for ResonantOS — canonical
source: https://github.com/KyaniteLabs/evo-x2-ec; this writeup is
non-canonical; where anything here disagrees with the canonical repo, the
canonical repo wins.
